subject: Post-demo: Evaluation charter & POC timeline for SkyQuest
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@skyquest.ai>
Cc: Ava Li <ava.li@skyquest.ai>, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 20 Feb 2027 15:08:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo: Evaluation charter & POC timeline for SkyQuest

Hi Daniel / Ava —

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier today. I wanted to recap the things we agreed on, outline a lightweight evaluation charter you can use internally, and propose concrete next steps so we can get a short POC started next week. TL;DR: 3-week POC, clear success criteria, Redwood provides a sandbox instance + eval checklist.

What we discussed (short):
- Goal: Integrate Redwood Inference to serve customer support summarization and intent classification for SkyQuest’s support triage flow.
- Target throughput: ~120 req/min with median latency goal <= 300ms for 512-token responses.
- Data: de-identified support transcripts (sample size ~2k messages).
- Success metrics: accuracy on intent labels (macro F1 >= 0.88), mean latency <= 350ms under typical concurrency, and end-to-end daily cost under $X/token (we'll estimate).

Proposed POC plan (attached: SkyQuest_POC_Scope_v1.xlsx):
1) Week 0 (prep, 2 days): data handoff (S3 link), security checklist, sign off on scope and IP/NDAs.
2) Week 1 (integration): Redwood sandbox setup (private trial environment), ingest samples, baseline runs using our curated model variants.
3) Week 2 (tuning & eval): iterate on prompt templates, batching config, KV-cache warmup, and gather metrics; run eval harness (we'll share redwood-eval-checklist.md).
4) Week 3 (wrap, recommendations): performance tuning, cost/throughput tradeoffs, final report and suggested production deployment path.

Ownership:
- SkyQuest: Daniel (technical lead) + Ava (product owner) — provide samples, define acceptance criteria, and enable test accounts.
- Redwood: Camila (deal lead) — commercial coordination; Rishi (SE) — integration & benchmarks; Grace (CS) — success plan and onboarding.

Open questions for you to confirm:
- Do you have a preferred start date next week (Mon/Tue)?
- Any regulatory requirements we should include in the checklist (e.g., retention windows, pii scrub thresholds)?
- Who will own the S3 bucket / access permissions for sample data?

Next steps: if you confirm start date, Rishi will kick off the sandbox provisioning and send the intake form. I attached a draft POC scope and the eval checklist so you can share with your engineers / security.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this moving.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0146

Attachments: SkyQuest_POC_Scope_v1.xlsx (xlsx) — draft timeline & responsibilities; redwood-eval-checklist.md (md) — automated eval harness & metrics to collect
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@skyquest.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ava Li <ava.li@skyquest.ai>
Date: Sun, 21 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Evaluation charter & POC timeline for SkyQuest

Camila — thanks for the recap and the clear plan. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

1) Start date: Tuesday 2027-02-23 works better for our infra team.
2) Data: we will provide a de-identified S3 link (we scrub PII server-side). Do you need IAM role access or temporary credentials?
3) Security: we need to confirm encryption-in-transit and at-rest, and whether logs can be forwarded to our Splunk instance for the duration of the POC.
4) Success criteria: the F1 target looks reasonable; can you add an evaluation slice for low-frequency intents (those with <1% prevalence)?

Also looping in Ava for product signoff. We'll review the attachments and get back with any redlines.

Thanks,
Daniel
Director, Engineering — Platform
SkyQuest Analytics

Hi Daniel / Ava —

Thanks — confirmed we can start Tuesday 2027-02-23. A few technical notes and what I need to provision the sandbox: 

What I need from SkyQuest before Tues (please):
- S3 sample bundle (presigned URL or cross-account role) with README.csv describing columns and label schema.
- A small baseline mapping table for intent labels (so we can map SkyQuest labels to eval taxonomy).
- Any IP/NDAs uploaded to the HubSpot deal or send to camila.reyes@redwood.ai.

Security & logging:
- Sandbox will be spun up in a dedicated VPC with TLS 1.2+, and data at rest encrypted with customer-provided KMS key if you choose.
- We can forward request/response logs to your Splunk via a secure forwarder for the POC window; we'll redact tokens and any fields you mark as PII in README.csv.

Evaluation specifics we’ll run out of the box (this is what redwood-eval-checklist.md covers):
- Macro/micro F1 for top-level intents, per-intent precision/recall, latency distribution (p50/p95/p99), throughput under two load profiles, and cost-per-1k-tokens estimate.
- Low-frequency slice: we'll compute sample-weighted metrics and also report per-intent sample counts; if any label has <50 examples we’ll flag it in the report and compute bootstrapped confidence intervals.

Provisioning plan (high level):
- Tue AM: sandbox instance + test API keys (Rishi)
- Tue afternoon: baseline inference run on 200-sample subset; share initial metrics
- Wed–Thu: tuning loop with prompt tweaks, batching and quantization profile; collect 1k-sample eval and tune
- Fri: final metrics and recommendations

I attached the intake checklist and the minimal config we’ll use (see attachments via Camila). If you want us to use your KMS key, please provide the ARN; otherwise we’ll use a temporary Redwood-managed key for the POC.

If everything looks okay I’ll begin provisioning early Tue.

Cheers,
Rishi Malhotra
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
